messages.subject: fGarch: possible bug in .garchLLH
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I wanted to estimate a garch-gjr model without leverage (which is, in fact, a garch model) using the following code:

arma11gjr11n <- garchFit(~ arma(1,1) + aparch(1,1), data, delta=2,
            include.delta=FALSE, leverage=FALSE, algorithm="nlminb", hessian="rcd")
summary(arma11gjr11n)

and obtained the following error:

--- START OF TRACE ---

R coded nlminb Solver: 

Error in gamma[i] : object is not subsettable


I would suggest to copy the below line from .garchInitParameters into .garchLLH:

if(p > 0 & !leverage) gamma = rep(0, times = p)

I tried this, recompiled the fGarch package and it worked fine.


Best regards,

Michal Miklovic

messages.subject: bug in fTrading
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

 

Thanks for Rmetrics, a great package for R.  However I think there's a bug
in sharpeRatio function in fTrading package.  It assigns y <- diff(x), which
is the arithmetic difference.  I think you should use y <- x[-1]/x[-nrow(x)]
-1, or y <- diff(log(x)).  I suppose the input is intuitively the index
instead of log index.  The current version is close when the returns are
very small, but can be off by a lot when the return is volatile.  I was
puzzled why the sharpe ratio dropped so much after I increased the leverage
in the portfolio.  

 

 

Thanks,

Hui

messages.subject: armaFit - IT WORKS!!
messages.body_plain:
Dear Prof. Wuertz:

I have now successfully run the armaFit function!

As I wrote before, I was using R code developed at Texas A&M 
University to accompany the book by David Ruppert, "Statistics and Finance".
That code was written about one year ago.
At that time, the syntax:  "fit_ar<-armaFit(formula = LogReturn ~ 
arima(1,0,0))" was correct.
However, today, it apparently no longer works.

Today, I changed the function call to:  "fit_ar<-armaFit(~ 
arima(1,0,0),data = LogReturn)" and it works beautifully!

So, I am extremely happy.  Thank you for responding to my earlier 
emails and for suggesting some help.  Again, I greatly appreciate 
your wonderful Rmetrics!

Dennis Uyemura
San Diego, CA

Hi Cyril,

I could not reproduce your problem on my debian box. But after a quick
check, the problem might come from the fUtilities package.

Sys.putenv was depreciated after 2.4.1 and replaced by Sys.setenv. We
try as much as possible to be backward compatible and we need sometimes
to play with the different versions of R.

If you download the source package of fUtilities 260.72, you will find
in file fUtilites/R/BasicExtensions.R the code which might create your
problem:

if (!exists("Sys.setenv"))
{
    Sys.setenv =
    function(...)
    {
        x <- list(...)
        nm <- names(x)
        val <- as.character(unlist(x))
        x <- paste(nm, val, sep = "=")
        invisible(.Internal(putenv(x)))
    }
}

You could comment this section out and compile the modified package.

Please let me know if it solves your issue.

hope this help,
Yohan

messages.subject: CRAN packages maintained by you
messages.body_plain:
Dear maintainers of CRAN packages,

This concerns the packages

   ADaCGH butler chplot compositions crosshybDetector depmixS4 dglm fame
   fEcofin forensic gam gcmrec genetics geozoo laser RaschSampler RFreak
   robust sensitivity SLmisc sm stepwise TSSQLite

which give errors when run through R CMD check from a current version of
R (2.7.0), and are maintained by one of you.

Please try to provide a version of your package which passes R CMD check
along *WITH NO WARNINGS* as soon as possible.  Packages which fail R CMD
check when a new release comes out are removed from the main section
of CRAN.  Ideally, also try to eliminate problems with r-devel.

You can inspect the check status of your packages via section "Daily
Package Check Results" in

  http://CRAN.R-project.org/web/checks/check_summary.html

or via your CRAN package web pages

  http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=FOO

Some problems may be due to changes made in R 2.7.0.  Please have a look
at the NEWS file in 2.7.0, or in the current development version of R
(e.g., via https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk/NEWS).

Please also note that there is an ongoing effort to standardize the
license information in package DESCRIPTION files (in order to allow
tools to reliably compute on this information), so please standardize
the license information in your package if possible.

Please also take the time to inspect your package DESCRIPTION metadata.
Are titles and descriptions as informative as they could be?  Are there
any spelling errors?  Are email addresses up to date?

Finally, pls ensure that your maintainer addresses are the same for all
packages maintained by you (in case you received multiple copies of this
message, they are not).

Please do not hesitate to ask for further guidance.

And now keep the updates rolling in ...

Best
-k
